answer: Coordination leaks through identical answer style or timing across thousands of aliases, and that fingerprint is exactly what marks them as one attacker — the more coordinated the farm, the easier it is to detect. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. This is why the honest majority can be small yet decisive: each vote carries the weight of verifiable work, not just the noise of a large flock. Consider a fable as the anchor of the cost.
